audit_status.source_base: Greek James text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact draft reviewed for favoritism, poor/rich reversal, royal law, mercy over judgment, trust and works, Abraham/Rahab examples.

verses.restored: My siblings, do not hold the trust of our Lord Jesus Messiah of glory with favoritism.

familiar.text: My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.

modern.text: My brothers, as you hold out your faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, do not show favoritism.

original.text: Ἀδελφοί μου, μὴ ἐν προσωπολημψίαις ἔχετε τὴν πίστιν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῆς δόξης;

verses.restored: For if a gold-ringed man in shining clothing enters your gathering, and a poor one in dirty clothing also enters,

familiar.text: For if there come unto your assembly a man with a gold ring, in goodly apparel, and there come in also a poor man in vile raiment;

modern.text: Suppose a man comes into your meeting wearing a gold ring and fine clothes, and a poor man in shabby clothes also comes in.

original.text: ἐὰν γὰρ εἰσέλθῃ ⸀εἰς συναγωγὴν ὑμῶν ἀνὴρ χρυσοδακτύλιος ἐν ἐσθῆτι λαμπρᾷ, εἰσέλθῃ δὲ καὶ πτωχὸς ἐν ῥυπαρᾷ ἐσθῆτι,

verses.restored: and you look upon the one wearing shining clothing and say, You sit here beautifully, and to the poor one you say, You stand there or Sit under my footstool,

familiar.text: And ye have respect to him that weareth the gay clothing, and say unto him, Sit thou here in a good place; and say to the poor, Stand thou there, or sit here under my footstool:

modern.text: If you lavish attention on the man in fine clothes and say, “Here is a seat of honor,” but say to the poor man, “You must stand” or “Sit at my feet,”

original.text: ⸂ἐπιβλέψητε δὲ⸃ ἐπὶ τὸν φοροῦντα τὴν ἐσθῆτα τὴν λαμπρὰν καὶ ⸀εἴπητε· Σὺ κάθου ὧδε καλῶς, καὶ τῷ πτωχῷ εἴπητε· Σὺ στῆθι ⸂ἢ κάθου ἐκεῖ⸃ ὑπὸ τὸ ὑποπόδιόν μου,

verses.restored: have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with harmful reasonings?

familiar.text: Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?

modern.text: have you not discriminated among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?

original.text: ⸀οὐ διεκρίθητε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς καὶ ἐγένεσθε κριταὶ διαλογισμῶν πονηρῶν;

verses.restored: Listen, my beloved siblings: did not the Divine choose the poor in the world to be rich in trust and heirs of the reign that he promised to those loving him?

familiar.text: Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?

modern.text: Listen, my beloved brothers: Has not God chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom He promised those who love Him?

original.text: ἀκούσατε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί. οὐχ ὁ θεὸς ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πτωχοὺς ⸂τῷ κόσμῳ⸃ πλουσίους ἐν πίστει καὶ κληρονόμους τῆς βασιλείας ἧς ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν;

verses.restored: But you dishonored the poor. Do not the rich oppress you and drag you into courts?

familiar.text: But ye have despised the poor. Do not rich men oppress you, and draw you before the judgment seats?

modern.text: But you have dishonored the poor. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into court?

original.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ ἠτιμάσατε τὸν πτωχόν. οὐχ οἱ πλούσιοι καταδυναστεύουσιν ὑμῶν, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἕλκουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς κριτήρια;

verses.restored: Do they not blaspheme the beautiful/good name called over you?

familiar.text: Do not they blaspheme that worthy name by the which ye are called?

modern.text: Are they not the ones who blaspheme the noble name by which you have been called?

original.text: οὐκ αὐτοὶ βλασφημοῦσιν τὸ καλὸν ὄνομα τὸ ἐπικληθὲν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς;

verses.restored: If indeed you fulfill royal Law according to the Scripture, You shall love your neighbor as yourself, you do beautifully/well.

familiar.text: If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well:

modern.text: If you really fulfill the royal law stated in Scripture, “Love your neighbor as yourself,” you are doing well.

original.text: Εἰ μέντοι νόμον τελεῖτε βασιλικὸν κατὰ τὴν γραφήν Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν, καλῶς ποιεῖτε·

verses.restored: But if you show favoritism, you work sin/misalignment, being exposed by the Law as transgressors.

familiar.text: But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.

modern.text: But if you show favoritism, you sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors.

original.text: εἰ δὲ προσωπολημπτεῖτε, ἁμαρτίαν ἐργάζεσθε, ἐλεγχόμενοι ὑπὸ τοῦ νόμου ὡς παραβάται.

verses.restored: For whoever keeps the whole Law but stumbles in one thing has become accountable for all.

familiar.text: For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.

modern.text: Whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles at just one point is guilty of breaking all of it.

original.text: ὅστις γὰρ ὅλον τὸν νόμον ⸂τηρήσῃ, πταίσῃ⸃ δὲ ἐν ἑνί, γέγονεν πάντων ἔνοχος.

verses.restored: For the One who said, Do not commit adultery, also said, Do not murder. If you do not commit adultery but murder, you have become transgressor of Law.

familiar.text: For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou commit no adultery, yet if thou kill, thou art become a transgressor of the law.

modern.text: For He who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” If you do not commit adultery, but do commit murder, you have become a lawbreaker.

original.text: ὁ γὰρ εἰπών· Μὴ ⸀μοιχεύσῃς εἶπεν καί· Μὴ ⸀φονεύσῃς· εἰ δὲ οὐ ⸂μοιχεύεις φονεύεις⸃ δέ, γέγονας παραβάτης νόμου.

verses.restored: So speak and so do as those about to be judged through Law of freedom.

familiar.text: So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.

modern.text: Speak and act as those who are going to be judged by the law that gives freedom.

original.text: οὕτως λαλεῖτε καὶ οὕτως ποιεῖτε ὡς διὰ νόμου ἐλευθερίας μέλλοντες κρίνεσθαι.

verses.restored: For judgment is without mercy to the one not doing mercy; mercy boasts over judgment.

familiar.text: For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.

modern.text: For judgment without mercy will be shown to anyone who has not been merciful. Mercy triumphs over judgment. Faith and Works (Galatians 3:1–9)

original.text: ἡ γὰρ κρίσις ἀνέλεος τῷ μὴ ποιήσαντι ἔλεος· κατακαυχᾶται ⸀ἔλεος κρίσεως.

verses.restored: What benefit, my siblings, if someone says one has trust but does not have works? Is the trust able to save/heal that one?

familiar.text: What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?

modern.text: What good is it, my brothers, if someone claims to have faith, but has no deeds? Can such faith save him?

original.text: ⸀Τί ὄφελος, ἀδελφοί μου, ἐὰν πίστιν λέγῃ τις ἔχειν ἔργα δὲ μὴ ἔχῃ; μὴ δύναται ἡ πίστις σῶσαι αὐτόν;

verses.restored: If a sibling is naked and lacking daily food,

familiar.text: If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food,

modern.text: Suppose a brother or sister is without clothes and daily food.

original.text: ⸀ἐὰν ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἀδελφὴ γυμνοὶ ὑπάρχωσιν καὶ ⸀λειπόμενοι τῆς ἐφημέρου τροφῆς,

verses.restored: and one of you says to them, Go in peace, be warmed and filled, but you do not give the things needful for the body, what benefit?

familiar.text: And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?

modern.text: If one of you tells him, “Go in peace; stay warm and well fed,” but does not provide for his physical needs, what good is that?

original.text: εἴπῃ δέ τις αὐτοῖς ἐξ ὑμῶν· Ὑπάγετε ἐν εἰρήνῃ, θερμαίνεσθε καὶ χορτάζεσθε, μὴ δῶτε δὲ αὐτοῖς τὰ ἐπιτήδεια τοῦ σώματος, ⸀τί ὄφελος;

verses.restored: So also trust, if it does not have works, is dead by itself.

familiar.text: Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.

modern.text: So too, faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead.

original.text: οὕτως καὶ ἡ πίστις, ἐὰν μὴ ⸂ἔχῃ ἔργα⸃, νεκρά ἐστιν καθʼ ἑαυτήν.

verses.restored: But someone will say, You have trust, and I have works. Show me your trust apart from works, and I will show you trust by my works.

familiar.text: Yea, a man may say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.

modern.text: But someone will say, “You have faith and I have deeds.” Show me your faith without deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds.

original.text: Ἀλλʼ ἐρεῖ τις· Σὺ πίστιν ἔχεις κἀγὼ ἔργα ἔχω. δεῖξόν μοι τὴν πίστιν σου ⸀χωρὶς τῶν ⸀ἔργων, κἀγώ ⸂σοι δείξω⸃ ἐκ τῶν ἔργων μου τὴν ⸀πίστιν.

verses.restored: You trust that Divine is one; you do beautifully. Even the daimons trust and shudder.

familiar.text: Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.

modern.text: You believe that God is one. Good for you! Even the demons believe that—and shudder.

original.text: σὺ πιστεύεις ὅτι ⸂εἷς ἐστιν ὁ θεός⸃; καλῶς ποιεῖς· καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια πιστεύουσιν καὶ φρίσσουσιν.

verses.restored: But do you want to know, empty human, that trust apart from works is inactive?

familiar.text: But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?

modern.text: O foolish man, do you want evidence that faith without deeds is worthless?

original.text: θέλεις δὲ γνῶναι, ὦ ἄνθρωπε κενέ, ὅτι ἡ πίστις χωρὶς τῶν ἔργων ⸀ἀργή ἐστιν;

verses.restored: Was not Abraham our father made righteous/just by works, offering Isaac his son upon the altar?

familiar.text: Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?

modern.text: Was not our father Abraham justified by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?

original.text: Ἀβραὰμ ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ἀνενέγκας Ἰσαὰκ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον;

verses.restored: You see that trust was working together with his works, and by the works the trust was completed.

familiar.text: Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?

modern.text: You see that his faith was working with his actions, and his faith was perfected by what he did.

original.text: βλέπεις ὅτι ἡ πίστις συνήργει τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἔργων ἡ πίστις ἐτελειώθη,

verses.restored: And the Scripture was fulfilled saying, Abraham trusted the Divine, and it was counted to him as righteousness/justice, and he was called friend of the Divine.

familiar.text: And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.

modern.text: And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,” and he was called a friend of God.

original.text: καὶ ἐπληρώθη ἡ γραφὴ ἡ λέγουσα· Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην, καὶ φίλος θεοῦ ἐκλήθη.

verses.restored: You see that a human is made righteous/just by works and not by trust alone.

familiar.text: Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.

modern.text: As you can see, a man is justified by his deeds and not by faith alone.

original.text: ⸀ὁρᾶτε ὅτι ἐξ ἔργων δικαιοῦται ἄνθρωπος καὶ οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως μόνον.

verses.restored: And likewise also Rahab the sex worker, was she not made righteous/just by works, having welcomed the messengers and sent them out by another way?

familiar.text: Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?

modern.text: In the same way, was not even Rahab the prostitute justified by her actions when she welcomed the spies and sent them off on another route?

original.text: ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ῥαὰβ ἡ πόρνη οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ὑποδεξαμένη τοὺς ἀγγέλους καὶ ἑτέρᾳ ὁδῷ ἐκβαλοῦσα;

verses.restored: For just as the body apart from spirit/breath is dead, so also trust apart from works is dead.

familiar.text: For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

modern.text: As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.

original.text: ὥσπερ ⸀γὰρ τὸ σῶμα χωρὶς πνεύματος νεκρόν ἐστιν, οὕτως καὶ ἡ πίστις ⸀χωρὶς ἔργων νεκρά ἐστιν.

translation_notes: James 2 is anti-favoritism and materially concrete: bodily need cannot be answered by words alone.
Trust and works are not abstract theological opponents here; living trust is completed in embodied action.
Rahab is named without sanitizing her status; her agency and hospitality are honored.
